A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 30-page documents, including Appendices A–D. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original random-feature measurements, Llama scaling and linear-probing experiments, and ViT classification results, including Figures 1, 3–5 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, together with estimator validation, test-loss scaling and explicit eNTK measurements in the appendices.

M1.justification: The LNP decomposition, spectral-position diagnostic and gradient-based computation procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic Gaussian teacher–student data, SimpleStories next-token prediction, and CIFAR-5M next-pixel prediction and image classification. No task or dataset coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain the same pretrained and random backbones, full training and frozen-backbone probes, and standard versus muP parameterizations. Comparator membership is unchanged in Figures 4, 5 and 9.

E3.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same model configurations, training budgets, data processing, measurement windows and evaluation procedures. Figure 9's corrected axis terminology does not introduce a different metric.

E4.justification: Linear probing, estimator convergence, isocompute comparisons, muP controls and explicit eNTK analysis are retained. The Appendix D.5 passage moving between pages 29 and 28 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 seeds for random-feature experiments, three initializations for the main scaling experiments, and 50 runs with standard-deviation bars for estimator convergence. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 9 changes the compute coordinates of smoothed spectral-position traces while retaining the raw measurements. For example, the 9.4M standard ViT smoothed endpoint moves from approximately 4.2e16 to 6.2e16 FLOPs at the same spectral-position value. This limited plotted-result revision does not establish improved performance; textual findings and other result figures remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same mathematical definitions and derivations, including minibatch normalization, the kernel-alignment relationship and random-feature scaling predictions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same claims about scalable spectral-position measurement, greater spectral reach in larger models and the enabling role of feature learning.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations, causal qualifications and limitations in Sections 5–7 are unchanged. Appendix D.5's explanation of the constrained eigendecomposition experiment is retained verbatim despite pagination changes.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, computational-overhead estimates and measurement instructions in Appendices B–C are unchanged. The Software and Data disclosures and associated resource links are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged, including positioning relative to kernel alignment, spectral bias and theoretical scaling explanations.

P1.justification: The preprint date changes from June 1 to August 4, 2026, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Body prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 9 is redrawn with χpos replacing χalign, common vertical scales across corresponding panels, revised tick formatting, tighter spacing and adjusted curve overlays. Its reduced height moves existing Appendix D.5 text onto page 28. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 9's χalign labels to χpos removes an inconsistency with its caption and the defined diagnostic. The common scales also make the standard/muP comparison clearer. These provide a limited improvement in presentation; the methods, theory, empirical support and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
